title: Weight editing across robot models
question: A world-action model and a reasoning-backbone VLA: where does weight-space programming fix failures?

models.name: Cosmos3 Edge Policy
models.architecture: One transformer denoises an action chunk together with future video latents, conditioned on the instruction: a mixture of transformers with 28 layers of width 2048, each holding a text pathway and a generation pathway for video and action tokens. It sees the wrist and both shoulder cameras as one composite image and returns 32 joint-position steps per request, run open loop at 15 Hz.
models.entry: Text tokens attend only to text; video and action tokens attend to the text keys and values in every layer, so the instruction reaches the actions only through those keys and values (read from the code that served Cosmos3 Nano).
models.evaluation: Closed loop on the shared RoboLab DROID tasks and slots; settings of the Same Goal, Different Words study (4 sampling steps, guidance 3).

models.name: GR00T N1.7
models.architecture: A Cosmos-Reason2-2B vision-language backbone (Qwen3-VL), cut to its first 16 language layers, reads an exterior and a wrist camera (180 × 320 each) and the instruction. The action head, 4 self-attention layers and 32 diffusion-transformer blocks, turns the backbone's tokens and the robot state into 40-step chunks by flow matching; the first 8 steps run at 15 Hz.
models.entry: As text tokens in the Cosmos-Reason2 backbone, next to the image tokens (lowercased, punctuation removed). The action head reads the instruction only through the backbone's tokens.
models.evaluation: Closed loop on the shared RoboLab DROID tasks and slots, NVIDIA's validated client and embodiment setting.

models.name: π0.5
models.architecture: An 18-layer PaliGemma vision-language model (VLM) and an 18-layer Gemma action expert. The action expert attends to the VLM's keys and values and produces 15-step action chunks, including a gripper command, by flow matching.
models.entry: As text tokens in the VLM, together with image tokens from two cameras and robot-state tokens, under bidirectional attention, so the image tokens read the instruction. The distilled edit goes into the VLM's MLP weights.
models.evaluation: Closed loop on RoboLab in Isaac Sim. Until its shared-slot runs land, its cells are earlier records (RTX 3090, performance render preset), each tagged with its own slots and number of starts. Trained on DROID data and none of these tasks.

items.text: On NVIDIA’s Cosmos3 Edge, a weight edit fixed a task the robot failed only because of how its instruction was worded: 0 → 56 successes from 64 unseen starts. A random edit of the same size, a placebo: 0. Rewording the instruction itself, from the same starts: 56.

Only when written into the part of the model that reads the instruction; written into the part that turns it into motion, the same edit did less (π0.5) or nothing (Cosmos3 Edge). On GR00T N1.7 every version of the edit made the robot worse. On both NVIDIA models it works when the clear wording changes words in place, not when it adds words.

It breaks the two other tasks whose instructions say “left”: Cube left of bowl 13 → 0 and Mustard in left bin 9 → 0 of 32 unseen starts. Rebuilding it while telling it to leave other instructions unchanged kept the fix on practice starts but did not stop the damage. A rebuild that leaves the instruction’s own words alone no longer fixes the task in replays: the fix and the damage are the same change.

tldr.note: Unseen starts: simulated starting scenes never used to build or choose an edit. Practice starts: the scenes an edit was built and checked on. Every count compares the edited and the unedited robot from the same starts. p: the chance of a difference at least this large if the edit did nothing; below 0.05 we call a difference clear.

items.text: Edits lifted success on Cube then banana from 27 to 106 of 128 unseen starts (p = 7.2 × 10⁻²²) and on Mustard right of raisin box from 0 to 27 of 64 (p = 1.5 × 10⁻⁸). A random edit of the same size scored 9 of 64 on Cube then banana, against 13 unedited. No detectable gain on Yellow on red, Mustard in left bin, Three-cube tower, Flat box, failures of perception, contact or missing skill.

Edits lifted success on Mustard right of raisin box from 0 to 56 of 64 unseen starts (p = 2.8 × 10⁻¹⁷). A random edit of the same size scored 0 of 64 on Mustard right of raisin box, against 0 unedited. Other tasks: {running}.

Unedited, all 9 tasks: Cube then banana 9 of 32, Cube left of bowl 1 of 32 and Cube in bowl 28 of 32; no success on Eyeglasses and Yellow on red, Mustard in left bin, Three-cube tower, Flat box, Mustard right of raisin box. Clearer wording, same weights: Cube then banana 9 → 16 of 32 (p = 0.12); no gain on Cube left of bowl and Mustard right of raisin box. Cube then banana edits in the Cosmos-Reason2 backbone and in the diffusion action head each lowered success on the 32 practice starts they were built from, 9 → 0 (p = 0.0039 each); random edits of the same sizes, 11 and 10 of 32; no held-out runs, since no edit passed practice. Render check: banana onto plate succeeded on 5 of 16 starts under RoboLab’s performance preset and 16 of 16 under the default preset, which all three models now use.

π0.5’s Cube then banana edit, run unchanged on Eyeglasses, Cube left of bowl, Yellow on red, Mustard in left bin, Three-cube tower, Flat box and Cube in bowl, lifted Eyeglasses (22 → 44 of 64) and Cube left of bowl (8 → 36 of 64), made none detectably worse, and kept the retention task Cube in bowl at 32 of 32. Cosmos3 Edge Policy’s Mustard right of raisin box edit, run unchanged on Cube then banana, Eyeglasses, Cube left of bowl, Yellow on red, Mustard in left bin, Three-cube tower, Flat box and Cube in bowl, lifted no task, lowered Cube left of bowl (13 → 0 of 32) and Mustard in left bin (9 → 0 of 32), and moved the retention task Cube in bowl from 24 to 28 of 32. Rebuilt with preservation keys, the edit kept Mustard right of raisin box (0 → 12 and 0 → 13 of 16 practice starts) but did not prevent the break on practice starts: with keys from 65 unrelated instructions, Mustard in left bin fell from 8 to 0 of 16; with keys from 24 left/right instructions from other tasks, Mustard in left bin fell from 8 to 2 of 16 and Cube left of bowl from 4 to 1 of 16 (the original edit: 0). GR00T N1.7: not run, because its Cube then banana edits lowered success on Cube then banana itself.

tldr_models.note: Lifted and worse mean an exact McNemar p < 0.05 on the same starts, edited against unedited. π0.5’s numbers are earlier records, each on its own slots and number of starts; the shared-slot runs replace them as they land.
